newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal prepares for municipal elections.
newsitem.headline: Senegal prepares for municipal elections.

text.p: Senegal holds municipal elections on Sunday with the ruling Socialist Party trying to recapture the urban vote that it lost to the opposition during presidential and parliamentary polls in 1993.
After a campaign coloured by predictions of official fraud, the interior ministry on Friday burnt surplus voting cards in front of the main opposition Senegalese Democratic Party (PDS).
"During the last elections we lost certain cities, this time, we say that will not happen again," said Bara Diouf, member of the ruling party campaign committee.
The opposition remains wary. "If the Socialist Party wants to divert the sovereignty of the people, the consequences would be incalculable," PDS leader Abdoulaye Wade said.
The opposition boycotted the last municipal polls, which took place in 1989 before Senegal's transition to more open multi-party politics.
Wade, defeated by President Abdou Diouf in disputed presidential elections in 1993, is running for the job of mayor of the capital Dakar.
He enjoys considerable support in Dakar and in the nearby manufacturing town of Thies. In 1993, his party also polled strongly in the towns of Kaolack and Saint Louis.
"The people of Dakar will be hard pushed to find a team that can do better than we have," outgoing mayor and Wade's main rival, Mamadou Diop, said.
Discontent after the 1993 polls flared into violent protest over the arrest of opposition activists in connection with the murder of the vice-president of the constitutional council.

Relations between Wade, who was himself detained for a time, and Diouf later thawed and in 1995 Wade joined the government as minister of state at the presidency where he has promoted a selection of economic projects such as a new airport for Dakar.
Diouf, whose seven-year mandate expires in the year 2000, is expected to stand for another term with Wade standing in a rerun of the 1993 poll.
Opposition suggestions of fraud ahead of Sunday's poll focused on extra voting cards.
The interior ministry, which runs elections in Senegal despite calls for an independent electoral commission, burnt 555,000 cards on Friday.
Just over three million voters are eligible to vote on Sunday, with 14 parties competing for for 826 regional council seats, 421 municipal council seats, 3,559 district seats and 15,386 rural seats.
Polls open at 8 a.m. (0800 GMT) and close at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT). First results and trends should be known within 24 hours. Final results could take a week to emerge.
